Key Takeaways

Pinterest closed at $18.96, down 19% in three months, near the $18.17 average price it paid for more than $2 billion of buybacks.

Third-quarter revenue grew 12% to $1.17 billion, missing its own guidance after EU rule changes cut cross-border seller ad spending.

Reddit plunged about 30% the same day after warning that Google's AI search is cutting its traffic, while Pinterest's users hit a record.

Pinterest's early February report must show fourth-quarter revenue near the top of its $1.425 billion to $1.475 billion guide.

Pinterest (PINS:NYSE) closed Friday at $18.96, down 4.2% on the day and 19% over three months. Earlier this year, it spent more than $2 billion buying back stock at an average of $18.17.

Oct. 30 hit two social platforms hard. Reddit (RDDT:NYSE) plunged about 30% after warning that Google's AI search features are cutting its referral traffic, while Pinterest slid on a revenue miss and a weak holiday guide.

The problems aren't the same. Reddit is losing visitors, with U.S. daily users down 2% to 50.7 million. Pinterest set a user record, and its weak spot was advertisers in Europe.

A customs rule cost three points

CEO Bill Ready blamed the European Union's removal of its de minimis exemption on low-value imports, which led cross-border sellers to cut ad spending. "The regulatory impact was greater than we anticipated," he said on the earnings call.

That pullback took about 3 points off global growth. The rest of the damage:

Revenue rose 12% to $1.17 billion, below Pinterest's own $1.19 billion to $1.21 billion range.

Europe revenue was flat at $193 million, with cross-border sellers an 11-point drag.

Adjusted EPS of $0.46 missed the $0.49 estimate.

Quarterly sales make the stall easy to spot…

Pinterest (PINS): total revenue, quarterly, $ billions, Q3 2024–Q3 2026 (TIKR)

Third-quarter revenue slipped below the second quarter's $1.18 billion, an unusual dip heading into the holidays.

Record users, flat monetization

Monthly active users reached a record 661 million, up 10%, with rest of world growing fastest. Revenue grew only a bit faster, so revenue per user barely moved.

Reddit shows the mirror image. Its revenue jumped 53% to $895 million even as U.S. users fell.

The fourth-quarter guide reflects Pinterest's strain. It expects revenue of $1.425 billion to $1.475 billion, up 8% to 12%, against a $1.52 billion consensus. Adjusted EBITDA is guided to $538 million to $588 million, below the $611.8 million estimate.

Ready called the range a "prudent baseline" and said cross-border pressure has stabilized. Analysts still model steady growth from here:

title: Reddit’s (RDDT) Short-Term Pains May Lead to Long-Term Gains

Reddit’s (RDDT) Short-Term Pains May Lead to Long-Term Gains

Reddit's (RDDT) short-term pains may lead to long-term gains, in my view. The leading social media platform lost more than 25% of its market value soon after it reported Q3 earnings on October 30. This crash followed traffic headwinds from Google's (GOOGL) AI Overviews and the rollout of its new artificial intelligence (AI) Mode features, which negatively impacted Reddit's user growth.

However, on November 4, Reddit stock surged 6% after the company announced that it is testing ad placements on Reddit search pages. This is a major step forward in monetizing its existing user base. The company is also planning to double down on forcing non-logged-in users to create accounts and log in to the platform. I am bullish on Reddit as I believe its recently announced strategies will trigger strong earnings growth.

Reddit Is Under Threat from AI

Although I am bullish on Reddit long term, there's no denying the company faces a major challenge as search engines embrace AI answers. The biggest culprit is Google. The aggressive rollout of AI Overview and AI Mode have fundamentally changed SEO principles. As confirmed by Reddit's management, Google continues to crawl Reddit to support AI answers. However, this does not translate into any user growth for Reddit.

Commenting on this during the Q3 earnings call, CEO Steven Huffman said, "Google is crawling us as hard as ever. So the demand hasn't changed from their point of view either. The reality is: the AI Mode does not drive traffic, not for us and not to anybody as far as I know. So it's just a fundamental shift in how Google works. It used to be a traffic driver. Now it's not. So now that changes the equation for sure."

Google search referrals have historically played a big role in Reddit's user growth. The company's user acquisition funnel usually begins with a Google query, which leads to a Reddit click, which results in a non-logged-in user acquisition. Over time, Reddit converts these users into logged-in users through its appeal. This business model is now under pressure, as AI Overview and AI Mode threaten the company's user-acquisition funnel.

Reddit Is Doubling Down on Monetization

One of the reasons behind my bullish stance on Reddit despite the threat posed by AI is the company's focus on improving monetization of its active users. The company is trying to achieve this objective in two ways. First, as CEO Huffman revealed on the Q3 earnings call, Reddit is gradually transitioning to a fully logged-in-only experience. The company is initially testing this in select markets outside the United States.

title: Do You Like Cash? Consider Reddit Stock

Do You Like Cash? Consider Reddit Stock

Reddit (RDDT) offers investors more cash for its price than most large companies. Its free cash flow yield sits at 6.1%, compared with 4.1% for the median S&P 500 company. That valuation follows a hard year, as Reddit stock fell 45.7% in the twelve months to November 4 while the S&P 500 returned 14.9%. Cheap cash means either a bargain or a business investors expect to shrink. So which is it for Reddit?

Reddit's Sales And Cash Are Still Growing Fast

So far, Reddit's figures lean to the bargain side. Revenue rose 62.2% over the twelve months to September from the twelve months before, and free cash flow reached $1.2 billion, up from $510 million a year earlier.

Shareholders own a piece of the free cash Reddit produces whether or not it is paid out, just as they own a share of its profit. When investors start to value that cash, the share price tends to rise, more so when the cash is growing.

Reddit generates that cash through advertising. Ads accounted for $847 million of its $895 million in third-quarter revenue. The platform requires very little equipment, and capital spending came to 0.55% of its cash from operations over the past twelve months. Its operating margin over that period was 29.4%, up from 13.8% a year earlier. Twelve-month free cash flow has risen at every quarter end since September 2023, when it was still below zero.

The company also owes almost nothing. Reddit ended September with $31.4 million of debt against $3.03 billion of cash and short-term investments, leaving lenders with little claim on what the business makes.

Reddit Warns Daily Users Could Fall In Q4

The risk Reddit named on its October 29 call centers on users, not cash. Management said search referral traffic fell meaningfully in the third quarter and dropped by an average of more than 1 million referrals a week in October. If that pace continues, management said daily users could fall by a low double-digit percentage in the fourth quarter from 130 million.

The share price appears to assume fewer users will cost Reddit revenue, but so far the drop in daily users remains a forecast rather than a result. Management did say total sessions are down because of the decline in search referral traffic, and the stock fell 29% on October 30, the day after that call. News reports that day also blamed a revenue outlook that came in below Wall Street's expectations. Management expects fourth-quarter revenue of $1 billion to $1.03 billion. That would be 38% to 42% more than a year earlier, slower than the 53% growth Reddit reported for the third quarter, but still growth.

Reddit Sinks 8% as Social Ad Worries Deepen in Tech Rout ©Brett Jordan from Pexels via Canva and sasirin pamai's Images via Canva
Key Takeaways

Reddit shares fell 8% today after Snap reported just 4% ad revenue growth, in a broad tech selloff.

Meta's 26% revenue growth last quarter suggests advertisers are still spending on the biggest social platform, so Snap's slowdown looks like Snap's own problem.

Reddit's bigger risk is the search traffic it's losing to AI answers on Alphabet's Google, which is why its fourth-quarter guidance disappointed.

The next big test for Reddit is its data-licensing renewal with Google, due in early 2027.

Reddit (RDDT:NYSE) sank 8% today. A weak quarter from Snap and a broad tech rout hit a stock that was already reeling from its own disappointing outlook.

Snap's ad revenue grew just 4% in the third quarter, and CEO Evan Spiegel said on its call that "advertising revenue growth remains below our ambitions." That's an ugly line for any ad-funded social app. But Meta Platforms (META:NASDAQ), the biggest of them, is telling a different story. And Reddit's real headache is still the traffic it's losing to Alphabet (GOOGL:NASDAQ).

Snap's problem looks like Snap's

Snap tied a drop in brand advertising to consumer packaged goods companies spending less. Meta isn't seeing that. Its third-quarter revenue rose 26% to $64.6 billion, and it guided to $73 billion to $76 billion of fourth-quarter revenue. Meta shares are down 4% today, less than QQQ's 6% drop.

Reddit's own sales haven't cracked either: revenue rose 53% to $895 million in the third quarter.

The bigger worry is Google

Last week, Reddit said its search referral traffic fell meaningfully in the third quarter. It also guided fourth-quarter revenue to $1.00 billion to $1.03 billion, short of what analysts expected. CEO Steve Huffman blamed AI Overviews and AI Mode in Google Search.

Those searches haven't gone away. Alphabet's third-quarter Search & other revenue rose 12% to $63.4 billion, and CEO Sundar Pichai said Google's query growth was "the highest it's been in the last five years." Alphabet shares are down 2% today.

Analysts still expect Reddit's revenue to keep climbing fast through 2028.

Reddit (RDDT): revenue, actual and consensus estimates, $ billions, fiscal 2024-2028 (TIKR)

I don't see Snap's quarter changing those estimates much, because Reddit's own fourth-quarter guidance still implies growth of roughly 38% to 42%. Google could change them. Analysts have already trimmed their 2027 revenue estimate to $4.34 billion, from $4.47 billion in late October.
